entities.name: Thulatthana of Anuradhapura
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Thulatthana briefly ascended to the throne of the Kingdom of Anuradhapura in 119 BCE, a pivotal year marked by intense dynastic struggle within the illustrious Mahavamsa chronicle. As a son of the revered King Saddha Tissa and a brother to three other future monarchs—Lanja Tissa, Khallata Naga, and Valagamba—Thulatthana's reign, though short-lived, represents a crucial episode in the turbulent succession politics that characterized the Anuradhapura period in ancient Sri Lanka. His rule momentarily interrupted the direct lineage, highlighting the fragmented power dynamics among royal siblings following their father's death.

His ascension in 119 BCE was not one of peaceful inheritance but a swift, decisive move against his elder brother, Lanja Tissa, who was the rightful heir according to tradition. Thulatthana seized power, embodying the fierce competition for the Sinhala crown that often pitted royal brothers against each other in this era. The precise mechanisms of his coup remain scantily detailed in historical records, primarily the Mahavamsa, but it is understood to have been a forceful takeover, leading to a brief but significant disruption in the established order of succession.

Thulatthana's reign was ephemeral, lasting only a few months before Lanja Tissa, supported by loyal factions, reclaimed the throne. This rapid overthrow underscores the fragility of power obtained through usurpation and the enduring strength of traditional succession protocols even amidst dynastic strife. His brief rule, however, set a precedent for future internecine conflicts, demonstrating how personal ambition could temporarily destabilize the robust administrative and religious structures of the Anuradhapura kingdom, influencing subsequent power struggles that would plague the royal family.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Thulatthana's very brief and contested reign of a few months in 119 BCE serves as a notable example of dynastic instability within the Anuradhapura Kingdom, highlighting the challenges of succession following a powerful ruler. His usurpation and subsequent overthrow influenced the political landscape of the royal family for a short period.
